clue.text: Agrees Bill should have trousers

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill
cords are corduroy trousers

explanation.surface: Someone consents that Bill ought to be wearing trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: To accord is to be in agreement, so the verb in its third-person form matches 'agrees'.

clue.text: Mug repeatedly cheers choral work

indicators.note: repeatedly says the following word is used twice in a row

parts.note: a mug and a can are both drinking vessels
ta is British informal thanks, like cheers
the same word used a second time

explanation.surface: Someone raises a mug again and again with toasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a musical composition for voices, often with chorus and orchestra.

clue.text: Nymph appearing in promotional material for quarry?

parts.note: ore is what a quarry or mine yields
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: A nymph turning up in a quarry company's advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: An advertisement for a quarry's product would be an ore ad.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology an oread is a mountain nymph.

clue.text: Daughter is left to fool around in books

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
taken as written
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A daughter left at home to play about with her books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In books' flags that the answer is a literary word, found more in writing than in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To disport oneself is to frolic or amuse oneself playfully, a literary term.

clue.text: Pot: certain thing ineffectual people rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: in horse racing a nap is a tipster's most confident selection, a near certainty
wets are feeble, ineffectual people in British slang

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a sure thing that the feeble have turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: A nap is a racing tip the tipster thinks is a certainty; NAP and WETS together are reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A stewpan is a cooking vessel used for stewing, a kind of saucepan or pot.

clue.text: Garden implement right in drier surroundings

indicators.note: in puts one item inside the other

parts.note: a towel is something that dries
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A gardening tool kept correctly in a dry environment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drier' reads as a comparative adjective but is a noun, a thing that dries.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand tool with a pointed blade used for digging in gardens.

clue.text: Retiring comedian, stressed about source of humour

indicators.note: about means around, so the pieces enclose another

parts.note: a wit is a clever, funny person
drawn means tense and strained

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the first letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A comedian quitting the stage, worn out over where the jokes come from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like a comedian leaving work, but it is the adjective meaning shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring and withdrawn both describe a shy, reserved person who avoids company.

clue.text: Called in a group of soldiers to plan

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in puts one item inside the others

parts.note: the RE, Royal Engineers, are a corps of the British Army
rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: Soldiers summoned to make plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Called' reads as summoned, but it is telephoned; RE are the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange something is to organize or plan it in advance.

clue.text: Brandish weapon with energy over one of a theatrical disposition?

indicators.note: in a down entry over means placed above, so the earlier piece comes first

parts.note: to shake a weapon is to brandish it
a spear is a weapon
E is the symbol for energy
an means one

explanation.surface: A dramatic type waving a weapon energetically.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: someone devoted to the greatest playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespearean describes things related to the playwright, so a theatre lover could be so called, loosely.

clue.text: Survey part of cricket match involving clubs

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: six balls; a small part of a cricket match
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A survey of one portion of a cricket game that features golf clubs or bats.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside ONE OVER after its first three letters, making ONCE-OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A once-over is a quick inspection or look, the sense of a brief survey.

clue.text: When one may have studied fish tail?

parts.note: a school is a group of fish swimming together
a term is an end or limit, as the tail is the end of something

explanation.surface: A question about the time a fish's tail was studied.
explanation.definitionFit: A school term is the teaching period during which pupils attend lessons and study.

clue.text: Hard exercising with jacket half on

parts.note: a cardi is an informal British short form of cardigan, a knitted jacket

indicators.note: half asks for only part of the following word, here its opening portion

parts.note: the first of the two letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone working out strenuously with a jacket only half on.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardio is vigorous exercise that raises the heart rate, such as running or cycling.

clue.text: Confused Dane cornered by Claudius? There's the rubbing

indicators.note: being cornered by someone means being hemmed in on all sides, so one piece is surrounded

parts.note: Claudius is the king of Denmark in Shakespeare's Hamlet

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled up and must be rearranged

parts.note: the four letters of the word, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Hamlet, the bewildered Dane, trapped by his uncle Claudius, with a nod to his line 'there's the rub'.
explanation.walkthrough: The ending echoes Hamlet's soliloquy line 'ay, there's the rub', but here the rubbing is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneading is working dough or muscles by pressing and massaging, a form of rubbing.

clue.text: Touch thorax, gathering temperature for allergy treatment

parts.note: to pat is to touch lightly

indicators.note: gathering means collecting something in, so one word takes another inside it

parts.note: the thorax is the chest
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A doctor's instruction to touch the chest and take a temperature reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch test applies small amounts of possible allergens to the skin to diagnose a reaction; 'treatment' is used loosely for this procedure.

clue.text: One young guy coming in to copy enamelwork

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so these pieces go inside another

parts.note: a clone is an exact copy
I is the Roman numeral one
a son is a young male

explanation.surface: A young man arrives to imitate a piece of decorative work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copy' reads as a verb in the surface, but it supplies a noun for an exact duplicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloisonné is decorative enamel work in which colours are separated by thin metal strips.

clue.text: Fruit the writer tucked into now and later, after cooking

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other words
cooking transforms ingredients, so the collected letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the writer refers to the setter, me
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook slips a fruit into something being prepared, now and again later.
explanation.walkthrough: ME sits between 'now' and 'later', and all ten letters are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A watermelon is a large green-skinned fruit with sweet red flesh.

clue.text: See 16
Assistance in bringing up English children at first in troubled times

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the following word
troubled means disturbed, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: English children being brought up during difficult times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bringing up' suggests raising children, but it means vomiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Emetics are substances that induce vomiting, so they help someone bring up their stomach contents.

clue.text: Augment with bling, especially in a bracelet

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other

parts.note: a bangle is a rigid bracelet
ESP is the abbreviation for especially

explanation.surface: Adding sparkle with jewellery, particularly a bracelet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Especially' reads as emphasis in the surface, but it is a standard dictionary abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To bespangle is to cover or decorate with spangles, glittering ornaments, which is adding showy sparkle.

clue.text: Forecast for aircraft to sequester carbon

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: sequestering means isolating something inside, so one piece is shut within another

parts.note: a jet is an aircraft
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: An aviation outlook about planes capturing carbon emissions.
explanation.definitionFit: To project is to estimate future figures from present trends, which is to forecast.

clue.text: Unsophisticated lust about anything vulgar

indicators.note: about means around, so one word surrounds another

parts.note: to lech is to lust lewdly
owt is northern English dialect for anything; 'vulgar' here means in the speech of ordinary people

explanation.surface: Crude desire concerning anything coarse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vulgar' suggests crudeness, but it means vernacular: OWT is dialect for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-tech describes technology that is simple, basic and not advanced.

clue.text: Was dismissive of chap's second edition

parts.note: his means belonging to a chap
S is the abbreviation for second
ed is the abbreviation for edition

explanation.surface: Someone disparaged a man's revised second printing.
explanation.definitionFit: Audiences hiss to show scorn or disapproval, so hissing at something is dismissing it.

clue.text: Row after Irish festival gets more spirited

indicators.note: after tells us which piece is placed second in the sequence

parts.note: a feis is a traditional Irish festival of music and dance
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A quarrel following an Irish festival makes things livelier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Feisty means lively and spirited, so its comparative describes something with more spirit.

clue.text: Capital city, extravagant? Mostly sleeping

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top, extravagant
away can mean off in a doze or dream, not conscious

explanation.surface: A puzzled description of a capital: lavish, yet half asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition works by example: this Ontario city is the seat of Canada's national government.

clue.text: Figurative expression: very high note's brought about end of mirror

indicators.note: brought about means placed around, so the first pieces enclose another

parts.note: the top is the highest point
E is a musical note

indicators.note: end points to the last letter of the following word

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A singer's top note somehow causes a mirror to shatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note's' is 'note has'; R goes inside TOP E after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figure of speech, a word used in a non-literal, figurative way.

clue.text: Harness oil at sea for the most part

indicators.note: at sea means confused and lost, so the letters are put in disorder

parts.note: ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship's crew using harness oil while sailing, for the most part.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion's share is the largest portion of something, the greater part.

clue.text: See 10
Orchestra finally directs adopting C scales

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the last letter of the word

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: to send is to direct somewhere
taken as written

explanation.surface: An orchestra at last tackles scales in C major under its conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scales' looks like musical scales in the orchestral picture, but it is a verb meaning climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale is to climb, so scales and ascends both mean goes up.

clue.text: Dutch city, ancient city, realistic about introduction of tourism

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: Ur was an ancient Sumerian city
echt means genuine or authentic

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A travel brochure listing a Dutch city and an ancient one, with a down-to-earth take on tourism.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur, in ancient Mesopotamia, is the crossword's favourite ancient city; echt is a German borrowing meaning genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Utrecht is a city in the central Netherlands, capital of the province of the same name.
